title: Chi è là?
subtitle: Donna Elvira, Don Giovanni and Leporello: recitative from Don Giovanni, Act 1

passages.label: là? · Stelle! che vedo! · Don Giovanni! sei qui? · Via, cara Donna Elvira
Cosa puoi dire … per pena forse che t'amai cotanto · Pare un libro stampato!
Oh in quanto a questo ebbi le mie ragioni · E quali sono … le mie vendette
Eh via, siate più ragionevole · Salvo il vero · Ebben, fa presto! · Madama, veramente
Sciagurato! … l'iniquo fuggi! · Eh, consolatevi! … donnesche imprese (to the end)

licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score (sei qui; azion si nera; calmate questa collera, where the libretto has quella; del ciel; e lasci in preda, where the libretto has e mi lasci; per pena; Leporello's conciossiacosa quando fosse che Il quadro, as printed; fuggi! and m'inganno, printed without the accents of fuggì and ingannò). Elvira's Chi è, the first two words of her line Chi è là?, are sung in the last bar of No. 3 (Ah! chi mi dice mai) and are not in this score.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 38–41, the recitative between No. 3 and No. 4 (60 bars)
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the continuo each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, a separate sweep for marks, then checked bar by bar and checked again by a fresh checker. The continuo is printed on one bass staff and is written here in the piano's left hand. Where the print adds a note for the English words (Leporello, bar 24), the Italian rhythm is kept; in bar 32 the print gives Elvira a sixteenth too many, and the eighth on le is read as a sixteenth so the bar adds up. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Playback tempo: Free, as recitative is sung: played here at a speaking pace, ♩ = 87, from the median length of five recordings (Fricsay 1958 2:35, Giulini 1959 2:26, Böhm 1977 2:59, Haitink 1984 2:56, Karajan 1985 2:45; about 2¾ minutes).
